---
title: "Genomic or phenotypic selection?"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4, dpi = 110)
```

Genomic selection (GS) predicts each line's value from its markers, using a
model trained on lines that were genotyped *and* phenotyped. In a line
pipeline it can replace the preliminary yield trial (PYT): genotype every new
line, predict, and send the best predictions straight to the advanced trial.
That trades plot costs for genotyping costs, and a measured phenotype for a
prediction. Whether it pays depends on the price of genotyping and on how
accurate the predictions are, and accuracy depends on how much training data
you have.

This article builds both pipelines in AlphaSimR with `alphasim_program()`, so
it also shows how to write a scheme of your own that `line_pipeline()` does
not cover.

```{r setup, message = FALSE}
library(tidyagsim)
library(AlphaSimR)
library(ggplot2)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12))
```

## Founders with a SNP chip

`asr_founders()` takes a `setup` function for anything beyond the default
trait. Here we add a SNP chip of 50 markers per chromosome:

```{r}
founders <- asr_founders(
  n_founders = 60, n_chr = 10, seg_sites = 150,
  setup = function(SP) {
    SP$addTraitA(nQtlPerChr = 15)
    SP$setVarE(h2 = 0.3)
    SP$addSnpChip(nSnpPerChr = 50)
  }
)
```

## One program, two strategies

The program follows `line_pipeline()`: cross, advance by single-seed descent,
screen, advanced yield trial (AYT), release and recycle. The only difference
is the screen. With `strategy = "phenotypic"` every line gets one PYT plot,
which takes a field season.
With `"genomic"` every line is genotyped and ranked by an RR-BLUP model
trained on all AYT lines so far (the founders' phenotypes in the first
cycle). Genotyping and prediction fit in the off-season, so the genomic
pipeline skips the PYT year: 3.5 years per cycle instead of 4.5.
`train_cycles` limits the training set to the most recent cycles.

```{r}
program <- function(founders, SP, strategy, train_cycles, genotype_cost,
                    n_crosses = 30, per_cross = 15, n_ayt = 60, n_parents = 15, cycles = 4) {
  tracker <- asr_tracker(founders)
  plot_cost <- 15
  parents <- founders
  training <- list(setPheno(founders, reps = 8))     # founders evaluated like an AYT
  accuracy <- numeric()
  for (cycle in seq_len(cycles)) {
    lines <- self(randCross(parents, nCrosses = n_crosses), nProgeny = per_cross)
    for (g in 1:3) lines <- self(lines)
    if (strategy == "phenotypic") {
      lines <- setPheno(lines)                                   # one PYT plot per line
      screen_cost <- nInd(lines) * plot_cost
      score <- pheno(lines)
    } else {
      train <- do.call(c, tail(training, train_cycles))
      model <- RRBLUP(train)
      lines <- setEBV(lines, model)
      screen_cost <- nInd(lines) * genotype_cost
      score <- ebv(lines)
    }
    accuracy <- c(accuracy, cor(score, gv(lines)))
    ayt <- setPheno(selectInd(lines, n_ayt, use = if (strategy == "phenotypic") "pheno" else "ebv"),
                    reps = 8)                                     # 4 locations x 2 reps
    training <- c(training, list(ayt))
    parents <- selectInd(ayt, n_parents)
    released <- selectInd(ayt, 5)
    cost <- n_crosses * 25 + nInd(lines) * 3 * 2 + screen_cost + n_ayt * 8 * plot_cost
    # 2.5 years of nursery, then the PYT year (skipped by GS: genotyping fits in the off-season), then the AYT
    years_per_cycle <- if (strategy == "phenotypic") 4.5 else 3.5
    tracker$record(parents, year = cycle * years_per_cycle, cost = cost, released_lines = released)
  }
  asr_summary(tracker, accuracy = mean(accuracy))
}
```

`tracker$record()` stores each cycle's parents, cost and releases, and
`asr_summary()` turns the record into the standard breeding metrics. Now
make it a spec, with the strategy and the training window as the choices and
the genotyping price as an assumption:

```{r}
spec <- alphasim_program(program, strategy = tune(), train_cycles = tune(), genotype_cost = 20,
                         founders = founders)

designs <- rbind(
  data.frame(strategy = "phenotypic", train_cycles = 1),
  data.frame(strategy = "genomic", train_cycles = c(1, 2, 5))
)
reps <- sim_replicates(10, seed = 1, scenarios = sim_scenarios(genotype_cost = c(10, 25)))

res <- tune_grid(spec, reps, grid = designs,
                 metrics = sim_metric_set(release_gain, gain_per_year, accuracy, cost, gain_per_cost))
```

`train_cycles` does nothing in the phenotypic pipeline, so we run it once.
For GS, 1, 2 and 5 mean training on the last one or two batches of AYT data,
or on everything collected (four cycles plus the founders).

## Accuracy, gain and cost

```{r}
m <- collect_metrics(res, type = "wide")
m$design <- ifelse(m$strategy == "phenotypic", "PYT plots",
                   paste0("GS, train on last ", m$train_cycles))
m[m$.scenario == "genotype_cost=10", c("design", "accuracy", "release_gain", "release_gain_se", "gain_per_year")]
```

```{r, fig.alt = "Screening accuracy for PYT plots and for genomic selection with three training windows."}
acc <- m[m$.scenario == "genotype_cost=10", ]
ggplot(acc, aes(reorder(design, accuracy), accuracy)) +
  geom_col(fill = "#4C78A8") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = accuracy - accuracy_se, ymax = accuracy + accuracy_se), width = 0.2) +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Correlation of screen with true genetic value",
       title = "How well each screen ranks new lines")
```

```{r, fig.alt = "Gain per year and gain per thousand dollars for each design; gain per year is the same for both genotyping prices."}
long <- rbind(
  data.frame(m[, c("design", ".scenario")], measure = "Gain per year", value = m$gain_per_year,
             se = m$gain_per_year_se),
  data.frame(m[, c("design", ".scenario")], measure = "Gain per 1000 dollars", value = m$gain_per_cost,
             se = m$gain_per_cost_se)
)
long$price <- paste0("Genotyping $", sub("genotype_cost=", "", long$.scenario), " per line")
ggplot(long, aes(design, value, fill = price)) +
  geom_col(position = "dodge") +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = value - se, ymax = value + se), position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), width = 0.2) +
  facet_wrap(~measure, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

What the study shows for this program:

* **Prediction is about as accurate as one PYT plot.** With a single-plot
  heritability of 0.3, the RR-BLUP predictions rank new lines about as well
  as the PYT does, and the training window changes accuracy only a little.
* **Per cycle, the PYT wins. Per year, GS wins.** GS gives somewhat less
  gain per cycle, especially when trained on only the latest cycle. It saves
  a year every cycle, though, so its gain per year is higher once it trains on
  two or more cycles of data.
* **The price of genotyping decides the money question.** At 10 dollars a line,
  GS trained on enough data gives about as much gain per dollar as the PYT, or
  a little more. At 25 dollars a line it falls well behind. Somewhere between
  is the break-even price for this program. Rerun with your own costs to find
  yours.
* **The comparison is paired.** Both strategies start from the same founders
  on every seed, so differences between them are measured precisely even with
  ten replicates.

## Make it yours

The program is ordinary AlphaSimR code, so everything about it can change:

* Use GS to *shorten the cycle* as well. Select at F3 from predictions and
  recycle parents before the AYT. This is where GS usually gains most, and
  it only means changing the year recorded per cycle.
* Mix the two: genotype everything, keep a smaller PYT, and select on an
  index of phenotype and prediction.
* Tune `n_ayt`, `per_cross` or the marker density (`nSnpPerChr`) along with
  the strategy.
* Use your own marker data for founders through `asr_founders(haplotypes = )`.
